topics.core_competency: The learner compares the forms of business ownership and selects a suitable one

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know the legal forms of business ownership. (k, v)
Know the types of Limited Companies. (k, u)
Understand the characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of each form of business ownership. (k, u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners should study a range of case studies that illustrate different legal forms of business ownership. Working in groups, they should identify the different forms of business ownership and present these to the class in a range of ways.
Learners listen to a guest speaker who can describe types and characteristics of Limited Companies. a. single directorship by: - guarantee - shares b. Multiple directorship by: - guarantee - shares

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe how well learners identify two forms of business ownership in their community and summarise characteristics, advantages and disadvantages of each.
In groups, ask learners to write a report on what they would like to know further from a guest speaker to their class. Assess how relevant their questions and ideas are for further exploration.

topics.core_competency: The learner compares the forms of business ownership and selects a suitable one

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the process and benefits of a formalised business. (u)
know the requirements to register a business in the business community (k)
understand the indicators of a formalised business. (k)
follow the correct steps in registering a business (k)
know the limitations of formalising a business (u)
know the process of deregistering a business (k)
know the process of re-registering a business. (k)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners listen to a business owner talk about how they went about formalising their business. In groups, learners compose and then ask key questions to identify: - the requirements of registering a business - indicators of a formalised business. - steps in registering a business. - limitations for formalising a business

Groups of learners create a guide for a new business owner, outlining how to formalise their business. Guides to be shared with another group who evaluate its effectiveness in supporting them to formalise their business

Learners listen to and summarise a presentation of a Guest Speaker on: - registering a business, and then they ask questions. - de-registering a business - meaning - steps - re-registering a business - meaning - steps

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to work in groups to conduct a field study to establish the registered and non-registered businesses in the community, and then asses the quality of the report they write about this.
Ask learners to design a flow chart to illustrate how to register a business. Observe how accurate their chart is and how well it reflects what they have learnt.

topics.core_competency: The learner compares the forms of business ownership and selects a suitable one

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning and history of cooperatives in Uganda. (u)
know the principles and benefits of Cooperatives. (u, v, s)
know the types of Cooperatives in Uganda. (k)
understand the process of forming a cooperative. (k, v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners research and produce a time-line of history of cooperatives in Uganda.
Through their research into cooperatives, learners agree a definition of a cooperative, and consider their benefits.
In groups, learners plan an informative report on cooperatives in Uganda for an information evening for local businesses.

Learners consider key information needed to make their report informative: • history of Cooperatives in Uganda. • registration process • principles of Cooperatives • types of Cooperatives • challenges facing Cooperatives • possible solutions

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to conduct a field study around the school community in order to identify facilities which the government has provided. In conversation with learners, ask them to explain which of these facilities have had a particularly positive impact on learning and school improvement in general.

Challenge learners to write a letter to the local government, outlining some funds that they believe are required to improve their community. Observe how well learners are able to reasonably request such funds and how relevant they are to the needs of their community.

topic_metadata.topic_title: The Savings Credit and Cooperatives Societies (SACCOS)

topics.core_competency: The learner compares the forms of business ownership and selects a suitable one

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Understand financial cooperatives (SACCOs). (u)
know how SACCOs operate.(k, s, v)
appreciate the benefits of SACCOs. (u)
recognise challenges faced by SACCOs in Uganda and identify possible solutions to the challenges. (k)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners should investigate a case study about SACCOs that illustrates how SACCOs operate, the benefits of SACCOs and the challenges faced by SACCOs in Uganda. They should summarise their learning in a short paragraph.
As a group, learners discuss and agree the meaning and purpose of financial Cooperatives. Learners should list with examples the benefits of SACCOs.

In groups, learners work together to outline possible solutions to challenges that SACCOs face. They should present their solutions to the rest of the class, who then debate which solutions presented seem to be the most effective.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to visit a nearby SACCO and write a report on: - membership - savings - credit - benefits to members - challenges faced.
Read these reports to assess how well learners understand these features of a SACCO.

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products for sale.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: distinguish between human wants and needs. (u, gs)
understand the types of human wants. (k)
appreciate the characteristics of human wants. (k ,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners discuss the meaning of human wants and needs, and create a table that shows the different types of human wants and their characteristics. This table should be shared with the class, who should agree on the top 10 needs and wants for their class, compared to those of their wider school community.
Learners should consider the link between needs and wants, human rights and the 2030 sustainable development goals.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Learners write about their personal wants and compare this to their needs. In conversation with learners, discuss the difference between wants and needs to explore how well they understand the difference.

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products for sale.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand production. (u)
know the types and stages of production and describe the benefits of effective record keeping. (s, gs)
know the factors of production and their benefits. (u)
make a simple production plan for a given product, including a budget
use spreadsheets, books and calculators. (s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners study a range of photographs that demonstrate all types of production. They should categorise these where possible according to a range of criteria.
In groups, learners discuss the types and stages of production, agreeing on the factors of production and their benefits.
In groups, learners prepare a production plan for a given product and prepare to share their plan with another group for critical analysis, before creating a final version of their plan.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to produce an infographic or poster which illustrates contrasting features of production processes. Assess how well learners have understood the range of production processes by what features they choose to highlight on the poster/infographic.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Specialisation, Division of Labour and Diversification in Production

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products for sale.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the difference between specialisation and division of labour.(u)
appreciate the types of specialisation. (k,v)
appreciate the advantages and disadvantages of specialisation, division of labour and diversification. (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As a group, learners think of companies that specialise in certain products and services. The group then thinks of a product, e.g. a car, and considers how many specialist roles are involved in making a car, and the division of labour. Learners should think of a contrasting product and compare specialisms required. Are there any similarities?
Learners conduct some research into the division of labour and begin to explain the challenges and opportunities of working in this way.
As a group, learners identify the advantages and disadvantages of specialisation, division of labour and diversification, using either the example of the car or another one they agree upon.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to write in groups about the existence of specialisation, division of labour and diversification in their own school. Assess how well they have been able to identify features.

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products for sale.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know raw materials for producing a given product. (k)
understand factors considered when selecting raw materials for a product.(u, gs)
use raw materials in production. (u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners select a product and discuss how it is produced. They agree upon the raw materials required for producing a given product, and record the factors considered when selecting raw materials for producing a product. Groups explain their findings with the class and then work together in the production of the product, where possible, or explore a further example from a contrasting industry. Groups evaluate each other’s products and the effective use of raw materials.

Learners create a table of raw products and their uses now and in the past. They should consider what uses these raw materials could have in the future, particularly with reference to sustainable development.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to list the factors that influence the choice of raw materials in production and evaluate how well their list explains the key features discussed during the lesson.
Ask learners to write a report on the process of producing a certain product and assess how well they understand the complete process by exploring steps that they have described in their report.

topic_metadata.topic_title: Machinery, Equipment and Tools Used in Production

topics.core_competency: The learner produces quality products for sale.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Understand the factors considered when selecting machinery, equipment and tools for production. (u)
select appropriate machinery, equipment and tools for production. (u, gs)
use of appropriate machinery, equipment and tools for production. (s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Take learners out to a field within their community to identify machinery, equipment and tools used in production. In groups, learners discuss the effectiveness of the machinery, equipment and tools used and present an argument for and against these different uses to share with the rest of the class.
Learners conduct some research into machines and tools now and in the past. They should consider how and why uses have changed and make some predictions about future uses of these tools, if at all.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to explain the factors that influence the choice of machinery, tools and equipment used in production. Observe their conversations to check whether learners are able to make reasonable connections between tools etc. and different types of production.

topics.core_competency: The learner markets and sells products

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the differences between marketing and selling. (u)
create a simple marketing plan. (u, s, gs)
appreciate the importance of marketing in business. (u, v, gs)
understand the challenges faced during marketing. (u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: As a class, learners explore and discuss examples of marketing and selling strategies and materials. They should discuss what they have purchased recently and what effect marketing and selling may have had on their purchases.
In groups, learners create a marketing plan for a product they will need to market and sell at the local fete to raise money for their school.
Groups think about what needs to be included in their marketing plan, who they will market to and when their product will be sold.

Learners discuss ways to market and promote their product, then market their product and sell it at the local fete. They should think about different audiences or groups of likely purchasers in order to inform them how to design their marketing materials.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In groups, learners evaluate their market plan and the challenges they faced to market their product. In conversation, ask learners to explain the main challenges they faced.

topics.core_competency: The learner markets and sells products

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the importance of market research. (u)
design a market survey tool for a selected product. (s, gs)
carry out market research. (s)
write a market research reports. (s, u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Working in pairs, learners consider some evidence presented to them that evidences the impact of market research on sales and trading.

Learners read a range of market research documents and explore marketing tools. In groups, they critically review their effectiveness. Groups agree a list of key considerations for marketing to be effective.
In groups, learners consider a product and design a market survey tool and carry out market research on the product.
Groups prepare a summary report about the marketing of their product and present this to the class. Groups consider range of ways to creatively present this.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In groups, learners write a market research report and present it in class. Look at what learners produce and assess how well they have understood the process of conducting market research.

topics.core_competency: The learner markets and sells products

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the channels of distribution.(u)
appreciate the factors considered when selecting a distribution channel. (u)
select the most appropriate distribution channel to distribute the products. (s,u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners identify various channels of distribution for selected products in their community. They should discuss what differentiates between distribution channels and the types of products that suit each channel.

Pairs share with another pair what they have found out about the variety of distribution channels in Uganda and Eastern Africa. These new groups agree on key factors that are essential when selecting a distribution channel.

Learners should challenge each other to select a distribution channel for a range of contrasting products. They should explain their reasons for solutions to distribution and any the key factors that could present challenges to distribution.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In groups, learners write a report on a field study aimed at exploring channels of distribution. Learners should present key features of their case study to the rest of the class. Observe how well they highlight important features of what they discovered.

topics.core_competency: The learner markets and sells products

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the importance of advertising and sales promotion. (u)
use the correct methods for advertising and sales promotion. (k)
promote different products. (s, v, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners study a range of advertisements and research how they promote sales. Groups share these findings to the rest of the class.
As a class, a list is created of the range of methods used to advertise, including the challenges and opportunities for each method.

In groups, learners evaluate the effectiveness of each of these methods and rank them in order of effectiveness and share through role play the different methods of sales promotion e.g. personal selling etc.
In groups, learners design a poster to advertise a given product, considering the intended audience.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: In groups, learners identify the sales promotion methods used in their community and explain their advantages and disadvantages.

topics.core_competency: The learner markets and sells products

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the importance of consumer protection. (v, u)
appreciate methods of protecting consumers. (u, s)
know agents involved in consumer protection. (u)
know challenges encountered in enforcing consumer protection in Uganda and other countries. (u, s)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners study a range of case studies that illustrate how consumers are protected.
Learners identify from case studies reasons and methods of consumer protection. They explain this to the rest of the class.
Learners listen to a presentation from a guest speaker on consumer protection.
Learners should consider related challenges of consumer protection, outlining possible solutions to these challenges.
Learners should speak to business owners, if possible, to explore what challenges they have faced in relation to consumer protection.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to write a report to describe the presentation from a guest speaker on consumer protection. In conversation, ask learners to explain what they think the main challenges are in protecting consumers.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the evolution of money. (u)
appreciate advantages and disadvantages of barter exchange. (u, s, gs)
understand the meaning of money, and its forms and functions. (u)
save money and develop the culture of banking. (v, u)
Understand the meaning of banks and banking. (u)
Know types of banks. (k)
know the challenges faced by banks in Uganda. (s)
Suggest the solutions to challenges faced by banks. (u, s)
know the rights of bank customers

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners listen to a visitor from the banking world talk about the evolution and origins and the various forms of and functions of money. Learners tell each other what they have learnt about money and describe to each other qualities of good money.
In groups, learners consider barter exchange and role play a range of given scenarios that allow them to identify the advantages and disadvantages.

Learners should discuss what they know about savings. They should research, if possible, how the savings culture has developed through time and what opportunities and challenges may be faced in the future. They should compare savings of a business to family living.
Learners should explore to some extent different forms of money in Africa and how these forms have changed overtime.
In groups, learners list all the banks in the local community and surrounding areas. Learners discuss the purpose of the banks and agree the differences and similarities of the different banks.
In groups, learners discuss the importance of banking to business and share this with another group.
In groups, learners research the challenges faced by banks in Uganda and attempt to develop solutions to challenges faced by banks and the rights of bank customers.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to explain the advantages and disadvantages of barter exchange. In conversation, check that they understand the challenges of this system of money exchange.
In pairs, ask learners to produce a short role play that evidences their understanding of the savings culture – a conversation between a bank manager and a new investor, for example.

Ask learners to name the banks they know and explain the importance of these banks to the school. In conversation, ask them to describe what they believe to be the key features which differentiate between types of banks.
Ask learners to produce a table which outlines the rights of customers and how this may be in conflict with banks needing to make a profit. Observe how reasonable their ideas are.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning of a central bank. (u)
know the functions of the central bank, (k)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners read text on the meaning and functions of the central bank, discuss and present a summary of this to class.

Learners should compare the role of the central bank to that of more local banks and community saving schemes. Learners should investigate the origins of the Central Bank, identifying reasons for its development.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to produce a diagram which outlines the key functions of a central bank. Observe how well their diagrams describe important features.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know commercial banks. (u)
understand the role of commercial banks. (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, can learners describe any commercial banks they know? Can they explain what makes these banks commercial banks? Learners should compare commercial banks to other types of banks and consider in what situations a commercial bank is the best option.
Learners should discuss the role of commercial banks and conduct some research as to how this is different and the same across Uganda and Africa.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to write a job description for the manager of a commercial bank. Observe how well this job description illustrates key features of the way a commercial bank is organised.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: distinguish between different types of bank accounts. (u, s, gs)
know features of different accounts and the difference between investment and savings. (u)
use a cheque, for cash deposit and cash withdrawal. (u, s)
know the procedure for opening a bank account. (k)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners list all the types of bank accounts and share with the class. Learners then choose one type of bank account and identify the features of the account and create these to demonstrate with the class (a cheque, cash deposit and cash withdrawal slip).
In the group, learners discuss who would be able to open an account and why. They should list processes and systems for opening an account.
Learners should work in pairs to investigate the differences between investment and savings, describing situations where each is appropriate.

As a class, learners should discuss how to use a cheque and why they are useful, as well as the challenges that they present. Learners should link this to cash withdrawal slips and discuss the need to balance to cash flow and investment/ savings.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to demonstrate how to use a cheque, cash deposit and cash withdrawal slip. They should do this in a role play. Observe how well learners understand the process.

Challenge learners to produce a leaflet for a family that encourages them to open a bank account. In conversation, ask learners to explain why they think opening a bank account provides opportunities and security.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Understand the meaning of microfinance institutions. (u)
know the types of microfinance institutions. (u)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners discuss the meaning and role of microfinance institutions to small businesses.
In groups, learners list the types of microfinance institutions, providing examples that interest them from across Uganda.

Learners work in pairs to investigate different types of microfinance projects and businesses in Uganda. They should consider and write about how microfinance has given a small business or individual the opportunity that larger banks are not able to offer.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to identify microfinance institutions in their locality and explain their role in business. In conversation, ask learners to explain why they think microfinance institutions are important.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: Understand electronic banking (k)
identify electronic banking products. (k)
know the benefits and challenges of e-banking. (u, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners listen to a guest speaker describing modern technological trends in the banking industry. In groups, learners present a case for electronic banking and then use this to persuade a teacher who does not use electronic banking.
Learners discuss the term e-banking and further research examples of where this has been useful and detrimental in contrasting industries and businesses.

Learners should list different types of electronic banking products and services. They should look for examples of how these have been used in their community and report on which they think are the most useful in different situations.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Learners to produce a poster or infographic outlining the modern technological trends in the banking industry. Observe which key features are chosen for the poster so as to assess how well learners have understood technological advances.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates the importance of money and financial institutions in conducting business.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand what taxation is and its origin. (v, u)
distinguish key terms used in taxation. (u)
know the types of taxes.(k)
know the advantages and disadvantages of direct and indirect taxes. (u, s)
know the rights of a taxpayer (u, gs)
understand the obligations of a taxpayer. (k)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners read a text on the origin of taxation, e.g. in the Bible, Quran, historical background in Uganda, etc., and then discuss the origins in groups and present their findings. Learners should ask each other questions about these origins and have some debate on how the nature of taxation has changed over time.
In groups, learners study a range of articles about taxes that illustrate the different types. Groups identify and list and then share the different types of taxes.

In groups, learners discuss the advantages and disadvantages of direct and indirect taxes. They should search for examples at a local and national level and discuss the effects of these taxes on the community and government.

Groups research and discuss the rights and obligations of a taxpayer and present to class what they believe to be important features. Learners should ask each other questions about rights and obligations, discussing which obligations are the most challenging to satisfy.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to speak to members of their community about taxes and then present what they find to another learner. Each pair of learners should compose a short paragraph to summarise what they have found out. Review this paragraph to assess how well learners have understood how taxes work in the community.

Learners should prepare interview questions for taxpayers in local businesses to see if they understand their obligations. Groups share their findings. Observe the key features of what they share with the rest of the class to ascertain how well learners have understood the challenges of tax obligations.
